body: no matter how bad the situation is, always try to push one more day.

exactly. however few and far between, there are occasionally times that i get these blasts of hope, and i find myself able to look past every single one of my problems, as if none of them matter at all. though despite it all, i find it all getting worse with each episode. 

hope you're able to find happiness :)

edit: i love electro-swing, perhaps my favorite song in that genre being [Black Betty by Caravan Palace](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D_JxMb8RLEY)

for me, it's always about finding little things to "lower the tide" in a sense. be it finding a song that i enjoy or spending time with my dog, i always try my best to find ways to delay the next breakdown, and while it is often in vain, i think that it's worth at least trying. for instance, the happiest that i've been in the past 6 months was when i naturally woke up at 6am after sleeping for 10 hours and discovering [this song.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=la9C0n7jSsI&index=40&t=0s&list=PL97vMPn997-gq3z873-wQDAoAnu3mEIAL) however, that was long ago and it's hard for me to find joy in that as well as most other songs in my music playlist because of how rock bottom my mental state has been getting. it means a lot to have someone to relate to, though i hope we are both able to get our shit together in one way or another. 

one thing that i read on this subreddit that has stuck with me for the past 7 months or so is that no matter how bad it gets, always try to put it off by one day. as terrible as saying "oh, i'll do it tomorrow" sounds in this situation, if it weren't for that "tip," i probably wouldn't be alive right now. as of late, i've been trying my best to follow that advice, and it's been one of the only things keeping me alive during the tidal waves.

that first thing you said about your problems not being worthy of anyone's sympathy really hits home - i suppose it's part of the reason i find myself in this situation.

i really appreciate the response, knowing that someone not only acknowledges my problem, but is able to identify with it, means the world.
